response.sql:
WITH analysis_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    t.tradekind,
    COUNT(DISTINCT tr.transreg) AS distinct_trans_count
  FROM advancedbehavior ab
  JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg
  JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg
  GROUP BY t.tradekind
),
totals AS (
  SELECT SUM(CAST(distinct_trans_count AS NUMERIC)) AS total_count
  FROM analysis_counts
)
SELECT 
  ac.tradekind,
  ac.distinct_trans_count,
  CAST(ac.distinct_trans_count AS NUMERIC) / t.total_count AS ratio
FROM analysis_counts ac
CROSS JOIN totals t
ORDER BY ac.tradekind;

assumptions.assumption: All foreign key constraints are satisfied in the data: every advancedbehavior.translink references an existing transactionrecord.transreg, and every transactionrecord.trdref references an existing trader.tradereg. The INNER JOINs enforce this implicitly.
